title: Google's AlphaProof Nexus Solves 9 Erdős Problems Including 2 Open for 56 Years

tickers.name: Alphabet Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
DeepMind's new AI system has successfully resolved 44 previously open conjectures from the Online Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences. The results, published in the journal Science, demonstrate that the AlphaProof Nexus system can generate original mathematical knowledge rather than merely solving competition-level problems. To ensure accuracy, the system uses AI agents to search for proofs while the Lean proof assistant formally verifies each mathematical step, eliminating the reasoning errors often found in large language models.

The AI also solved 9 open problems posed by Paul Erdős, including 2 that had resisted mathematicians for 56 years. The system's architecture combines existing Gemini models with a specialized processing loop, and compute costs were reported at a few hundred dollars per problem. This announcement coincides with calls from some mathematicians to boycott OpenAI following a separate release of papers.

AI is now solving mathematical problems that have remained unsolved for more than half a century!

@GoogleDeepMind's AlphaProof Nexus has successfully solved 9 previously open Erdős problems, including two that had resisted mathematicians for 56 years. It also proved 44 previously open conjectures from the Online Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences.

The really exciting part is how it works. AI agents autonomously search for mathematical proofs, while the Lean proof assistant formally verifies their correctness. No relying on an LLM's word that its reasoning is sound.

The results have just been published in Science. We're moving beyond AI solving math competition problems to AI actually contributing new mathematical knowledge. And this is only the beginning!
